our_argument_summary: WIN-068 cites Kim & Chang (2018) Adv. Space Res. 61:2040-2049 as a retrospective 39-eclipse INTERMAGNET ensemble (1991-2016) whose perturbations are produced by the Chapman-Sq ionospheric mechanism (Chapman 1919; modern conductivity treatment Yamazaki & Maute 2017, SSR 206:299-405, DOI 10.1007/s11214-016-0282-z). We argue (1) non-discriminating — Chapman-Sq predicts the qualitative pattern without dome geometry; (2) post-hoc — Kim & Chang published 2018, dome incorporated V51.0 in 2026 (~8-year gap); (3) no dome-derived numerical prediction (FSF scaling enters only WIN-010 2026 forward projection, not 1991-2016 ensemble); (4) WIN-010 / WIN-025 / WIN-068 triple-count the same Chapman-Sq mechanism at three aggregation scales. Verdict: Std Model Explains. (c18: identical to c17 — patch did not alter argument structure.)

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: monitor.py contains no domain logic for WIN-068; the 39-eclipse ensemble is a retrospective literature citation with no live validation pipeline.

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: monitor.py searched for WIN-068, 068, eclipse-ensemble, and Kim-Chang token forms — no domain entry, no API call, no static observation, no comparison logic exists for this WIN. The dome incorporates Kim & Chang (2018) only as a confirmed-WIN claim in the published WIN list; no automation surface is present.
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Chapman (1919) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 218:1-118 first described the lunar-shadow → ionospheric Sq mechanism; Yamazaki & Maute (2017, SSR 206:299-405, DOI 10.1007/s11214-016-0282-z) gives the modern conductivity treatment; Kim & Chang (2018) verified the qualitative pattern across the 39-eclipse ensemble. Dome merely renames the same mechanism "pressurized toroidal cavity induction gradient" without introducing different numerical predictions.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Kim & Chang published 2018; dome incorporated V51.0 in 2026 — ~8-year gap. The dome adopts the already-confirmed ensemble result and labels it a confirmed prediction; no pre-registered ensemble amplitude in an independent venue predating publication has been located.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The 39-eclipse ensemble counted here invokes no FSF, no H(r), no disc-radius scaling. The dome's FSF scaling enters only the WIN-010 2026 forward projection, not the retrospective 1991-2016 ensemble. detail_evidence P4 and detail_verdict_text P2 explicitly carve this out.

holes_found.description: Carry-over from c17 H1 (still unresolved as of git HEAD cee80d3): finding wording "reproduces the 39-eclipse signal magnitude and geometry" overclaims a-priori predictive power. The detail_evidence P3 acknowledges Chapman-Sq predicts only the qualitative pattern (Y-component sign, X/Z/F sign, latitude peak, ~180-min timescale); detail_verdict_text P2-P3 concede that absolute ensemble amplitudes come from the 1991-2016 dataset itself, not from forward Chapman-Sq derivation. "Magnitude" attributes quantitative power that the framework does not have a priori — the magnitude lives in the empirical ensemble.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace "reproduces the 39-eclipse signal magnitude and geometry" with "explains the ensemble pattern (component signs, latitude peak, ~180-min timescale)" or "reproduces the qualitative ensemble pattern." Keeps the non-discriminating verdict intact while removing the residual a-priori-magnitude overclaim. Decider note: c17 already flagged this; c18 grades it as carry-over because no patch was applied between c17 (2026-06-16T05:15Z) and now. If decider already wontfix-rationaled this between runs, the wontfix recordation supersedes — please confirm in close-record.

kernel_of_truth.description: The patch (${CLONE}/data/wins.json:WIN-068.finding) correctly closes a real reviewer-credibility risk: a defender who spotted "2026 European cohort" in our summary-table finding could have argued that we cannot keep our own WIN list straight (WIN-025 is unambiguously the April 8, 2024 North American eclipse per wins.json:WIN-025.detail_evidence and Chernogor & Holub 2024 DOI 10.1016/j.asr.2024.10.056). Fixing it removes that vulnerability before any reader encounters it.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Fixing a one-line typo does not change the WIN-068 scientific verdict. The Chapman-Sq mechanism (raw-text/monitor.py: no domain entry; Yamazaki & Maute 2017 DOI 10.1007/s11214-016-0282-z) still predicts the qualitative pattern without dome parameters, and the 1991-2016 ensemble is still a post-hoc literature citation with monitoring="none" per code_analysis_tags above. The patch closes a presentation hole; the underlying "Std Model Explains" verdict (wins.json:WIN-068.verdict) is unmoved.
